units: Yoma IV, 2 פָּשַׁעְתִּי; ib. VI, 2 פָּשְׁעוּ, v. עָוָה; a. fr.—פּוֹשֵׁעַ a wilful transgressor, rebel, apostate.
<cite ref="Gittin 57a">Gitt. 57ᵃ</cite> <he>פ׳ ישראל</he> a Jewish apostate (the censor’s disguise for Jesus).
<cite ref="Gittin 57a:4">Ib.</cite> <he>תא חזי מה בין פּוֹשְׁעֵי ישראל וכ׳</he> come and see the difference between Jewish apostates and gentile prophets.

<cite ref="Rosh Hashanah 17a:3">R. Hash. 17ᵃ</cite> <he>פ׳ ישראל בגופן</he> Jewish sinners with their bodies (disregarding the ceremonial laws intended to guard the purity of life); <he>פ׳ אומות העולם בגופן</he> gentile sinners with their bodies (lustful and violent).

<cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 51:3">Midr. Till. to Ps. LI</cite> <he>כשאתה אומר לפּוֹשְׁעִים … אם תקבלני כל הפושעים משלימים לך</he> when thou sayest to the sinners, why have you not repented? (they may plead ignorance of thy goodness, but) if thou receivest me, all sinners will make peace with thee; a. fr.

Gen. R. s. 52 (ref. to Prov. XVIII, 19) פָּשַׁעְתָּ באברהם thou (Lot) wast faithless to Abraham; Num. R. s. 18 זה קרח שפ׳ בתורה וכ׳ this refers to Korah who was faithless to the Law, which is called ‘strength’; a. fr.—Esp. (with ref. to Ex. XXII, 8) to be negligent in guarding a trust.
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 36b:4">B. Mets. 36ᵇ</cite> <he>פ׳ בה וכ׳</he> if he was careless in guarding the animal, and it went out &c.
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 34a:9">Ib. 34ᵃ</cite> <he>כיון שאמר פשעתי וכ׳</he> as soon as he says, ‘I have been at fault’, he surrenders the eventual fine (of the thief) to the owner.
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 58a:2">Ib. 58ᵃ</cite> <he>כי היכי דלא לקרו להו פושעים</he> in order that they may not be called faithless guardians; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Berakhot 28a:14">Ber. 28ᵃ</cite> <he>ונקרא פושע</he> and he is called negligent (because he delayed his prayers).

<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 9:47">Num. R. s. 9</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Exodus 22:8">Ex. XXII, 8</cite>) <he>מדבר באהרן שה׳ ישראל בדיבור לא יהיה</he> it alludes to Aaron who caused Israel to transgress the commandment, ‘thou shalt have no other gods &c.’ (<cite ref="Exodus 20:3">Ex. XX, 3</cite>).
